name: Old California Botanicals
products: Heirloom and specialty citrus, including oranges, mandarins, tangelos, grapefruit, and lemons; aromatic and culinary botanicals; marmalades; essential oils; botanical fragrances; beeswax lip balms; and other value-added citrus and botanical products.
description: Old California Botanicals is a Redlands-based agricultural and botanical producer rooted in Southern California’s historic Citrus Belt. Drawing on five generations of local citrus-growing tradition, we practice regenerative agriculture with a focus on heirloom and uncommon citrus varieties and the preservation of California’s agricultural heritage. We grow and produce distinctive citrus, botanicals, and small-batch products including award-winning marmalades, essential oils, fragrances, and personal care goods. Our work combines cultivation, conservation, and value-added production to help keep historic varieties and agricultural traditions alive while demonstrating a productive future for small-scale Southern California agriculture.

name: Santa Cruz Permaculture Farm
products: Fruits, vegetables, flowers and herbs
description: Santa Cruz Permaculture is a small family farm committed to growing the most delicious, nutritious, high quality organic fruits, vegetables, flowers and herbs. While the land has been farmed organically for over 100 years, we are transitioning to a regenerative, organic, no-till, mixed vegetable, flower, fruit, herb, and agroforestry farm with a strong emphasis on education. We have over 1,000 alumni from our programs, and our farm aims to push the limits on regenerative agriculture to increase biodiversity, resilience, and community. We’re delighted to have such an incredibly beautiful and wild space to host our permaculture courses and farm events. Our students are welcome to camp during the weekends of their course and enjoy the peace and quiet, stargazing, community campfires, and the sound of the seals from nearby Ano Nuevo Island. We are a 26 acre regenerative organic farm 20 minutes north of Santa Cruz on the Pacific coast. We grow delicious and nutritious foods – over 80 crops – for our U-Pick, farm stand, farmers markets, online shop, Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) program, and caterers, restaurants and wholesale customers. The farm has 5 acres of mixed vegetables, flowers, and herbs, 2 acres of blackberries, 1/3 acre of kiwis, and 1 acre of basketry willows, and is the site for our many permaculture courses. We are establishing an extensive food forest orchard and watershed regeneration demonstration. We have an ocean view and access to Ano Nuevo Creek. We can see the ocean from our farm and it is a 10 minute walk to the sands of the state park beach.

We have been farming for five generations and have two decades of experience serving local students through Farm to School! We are here to provide our community – you guys – with the best fruits and vegetables we can grow, to take care of our land as true land stewards (we’re certified organic), and to connect kids with the wonder of nature!

Adam and Kristen McLane have a passion for educating the public regarding sustainable growing practices, native plant life, and food security. On their farm they grow a wide variety of seasonal vegetable crops, keep livestock like chickens and goats, offer locally adapted nursery starts, and grow a wide variety of microgreens. They are proud to grow in Mariposa County.

name: Pollinate Farm
products: Collards, kale, mustard, broccoli, okra, garlic, carrots, turnips radishes, cucumbers, squash, tomatoes, herbs, and flowers
description: For some, the draw of Home Grown Food is about reconnecting to our past. For others, it’s a way to ensure good food close to home. At Pollinate Farm we believe that everyone deserves food that is flavorful, nutritious and sustainably grown. Pollinate Farm is a Black Woman-owned microfarm in Oakland CA. It was born from a successful retail operation supporting, supplying and educating urban food growers. Our model is unique. We are a tapestry of urban growing sites, spread across several locations. Through the generosity of our neighbors, we are able to grow food in local residential spaces. Our farm sites are powered by an amazing team of volunteers from many professions. We grow fresh, healthy, local food for San Francisco and East Bay communities, without the carbon miles. We are stewarding the land and improving the biodiversity in the soil, one backyard at a time.

We grow over 20 culturally preferred vegetables and deliver them farm-to-door via our CSA project. Our CSA membership is diverse in socioeconomic background; we care about all people having access to fresh. organic vegetables. We also operate a small farm-to-cafeteria project with three local high schools. Finally we work closely with the 9 Organic Farmer Coop which supplies some produce to the CSA and F2C projects.

name: BURNS BLOSSOM FARM
products: Tomatoes, lettuce, strawberries, cucumbers, greens, garlic, cut-flowers, roots, hot sauce.
description: BURNS BLOSSOM is a REAL ORGANIC PROJECT & CCOF/USDA certified organic, diversified market farm under the stewardship of Mel & Kyle Forrest Burns(previously of Nye Ranch Farm). Farming is what we love, sharing and caring is what were best at! Our farming practices aim to maximize photosynthesis, increase the soil organic matter, sequester carbon, and nurture the community. Utilizing regenerative farming practices such as cover crops, mulching, intercropping, ramial wood-chip pathways, no-till practices, and pollinator hedgerows. We’re always trialing and experimenting with new techniques to foster soil health.

description: Farmboy Organics is a 12 acre certified organic diversified farm that grows vegetables, citrus and olive oil in Winters. We grow year-round with the summer heat creating deliciously sweet veggies and fruit while the cold but not too cold winter is perfect for citrus and winter veggies. Every fall we hand harvest olives and cold press them on the farm within 24 hours to have a peppery, buttery olive oil that is perfect with any dish. We sell our produce at the Davis Farmers Market on Saturdays and Wednesdays as well as to the Davis Food Co-op, Capay Valley Farm Shop, fruitqueen and local grocers and restaurants. Some of the crops we grow are; heirloom tomatoes, cherry tomatoes, early girl tomatoes, Melons, Nantes carrots, cucumbers, lettuce, potatoes, olive oil, grapefruit, eggplant, kale, beets, broccolini, yuzu, blood oranges, persimmons, pomegranates, figs, cabbage, spinach, broccoli, cauliflower, basil, peppers, okra, turnips.

description: Zava Ranch is a family-owned sustainable ethically-cultivated fruit orchard and herb garden on 20 acres in Somis, Ventura County, Southern California, USA. We are committed to partnering with nature to cultivate, grow, and harvest the most nutritious, delicious, and healing foods that our land is willing to share with us. We work with nature and follow its lead. California has many different microclimates. Our land gifts us fields of rosemary, sage, oregano, lavender, roses, geranium, hibiscus, and succulents. With some additional irrigation, it produces an abundance of lemons, limes, oranges, tangerines, grapefruit, and avocados.

Owners of Balakian Farms are members of the Balakian Family. In the 1990’s, the farm transitioned to organic practices, and began growing heirloom tomatoes. In the summer, you can find our produce and products at the Bay Area farmer’s markets and several retailers. Farming is more than an occupation for Balakian Farms: it is a way of life.

Being able to own land here on the Central Coast, much less farm it, is not easy to say the least.  We grow organic fruit, vegetables, and flowers on 200 acres in Monterey County – 120 acres are apart of a conservation easement.  With the partnership of the Elkhorn Slough Foundation we were able to make our dream of owning our farm reality. Our team is what makes JSM Organics a reality, we pride ourselves on taking care of one another.  Being happy, living well, and providing food for our communities.  The path that destiny had for me, makes me incredibly thankful that it led me back to farming. Thank you for supporting our family farm – we hope to see you soon at the market or here on the farm. Muchisimas Gracias

description: We are a small family farm partnered with Belden Barns on Sonoma Mountain outside of Santa Rosa, CA. We grow vegetables and tree fruit on four acres and follow all organic principles and practices. In our fields you’ll find everything from heirloom tomatoes and melons to lettuce and baby corn. We grow many kinds of specialty Asian vegetables as well as storage crops like heirloom dry beans, milling corn and popcorn. We work closely with chefs around the region to plan each season’s crop mix and trial new varieties. The orchard includes over 25 varieties of apples, with fruit chosen specially for cider, as well as over 30 varieties of pears, plums, peaches, quince, and assorted citrus. Almost everything we grow is available through the food hub F.E.E.D. Sonoma, California’s first farmer- and employee-owned fresh produce cooperative. We also sell some of our products under the Belden Barns label (including cider made from our fruit) and in partnership with local CSA farms.

description: The Peach Jamboree, nestled in the Sierra Foothills, is owned and operated by lifemates Danny and Drew. We are certified organic, grow peaches, pears, apples, and vegetables to sell at bay area farmers markets as well as host orchard dinners and celebratory gatherings onsite. Find us at the following Bay Area farmers markets during our harvest season: Tuesday – South Berkeley Thursday – North Berkeley Saturday – Chico, Ferry Plaza, Downtown Berkeley Sunday – Marin, Sebastopol Danny and Drew acquired Woodleaf Farm in winter 2015 when founder and owner Carl sold the farm after 35 years to start a new project. They hit the ground running to learn everything there was to know about running the farm, bringing collective decades of agriculture experience to the table. Danny and Drew renamed the farm The Peach Jamboree, with the intention of offering the space for orchard dinners, community gatherings, and other events

We also sell earth friendly Jams and Fruit Butters (Persimmon Butter, Spiced Pear, Mission Fig, Wild Sierra Plum, Wild Blackberry and Quince) from our orchard trees along with local Honey from our visiting Bees. Nature inspired Craft items and Ornaments, Persimmon Loaves, Cookies and Waffles with Hot Cider can complete your Fall outing to our Lean Two Cottage Food Stand. description: Dwelley Family Farms is a family owned 4th generation farm, growing in Brentwood since 1921. Dwelley Family Farms has taken great pride in offering a large variety of premium fruits and vegetables to its local and commercial customers. Brentwood’s unique microclimate of hot valley days combined with the cool coastal evening breezes creates a perfect condition for growing produce. Just on the outskirts of the metropolitan Bay Area, Dwelley Family Farms’ ideal location allows for the ability to offer the freshest of produce to this continually growing population. Best known for their sweet corn and green bean varieties, Dwelley Family Farms’ conventional and organic produce can be found at our local fruit stand or at retail outlets across the Bay Area. Sustainability has always been a primary focus of Dwelley Family Farms. Using responsible farming practices has enabled Dwelley Family Farms the ability to provide the healthiest quality and best tasting produce. It is said that for the entire Dwelley family, farming has never been just an occupation. It is a way of life!

name: Weiser Family Farms
products: Melons, grapes, peaches, stone fruit, peppers, tomatoes, potatoes, flowers, carrots, greens, radicchio, cauliflower, spinach, broccoli, cabbage
description: Weiser Family Farms began in 1977 when Sid Weiser, a chemistry teacher and counselor at Garfield High School in East Los Angeles decided to pack up the family and follow his dream of working off the land. Sidney and his wife Raquel laid down roots (if you will) in Tehachapi, California. There, they learned to tend to the fruit trees . . . apples, peaches, and pears. In the ensuing years, they acquired farmland in other locations where they branched out into a variety of fruits, vegetables, and flowers. In 1982 their son Alex jumped in to assist the family in selling at local Farmers’ Markets. There he encountered chefs, the public and specialty produce buyers who wanted seasonal, high quality and superior tasting produce. Listening to this input, Alex began to focus on creating a bio-diverse farm dedicated to applying sustainable farming techniques. His overriding desire was to supply people with unique fruits and vegetables at their peak, rather than picked for commercial usage. Today the Weiser family farms in the Greater Bakersfield area, Tehachapi and the Lucerne Valley, cultivating a tapestry of high quality produce year round. Older brother Dan joined the family business in 2001, after a long stint with The Walt Disney Co. Dan, a graduate of USC’s Marshall School of Business, brought with him a real world business sensibility to the farm that has helped bring the overall operation to the next level. Not long after Dan came aboard, older sister Esther left her established teaching career to help keep her knuckle-headed brothers in line. Her common sense approach and no nonsense communication style help to keep everything in focus and moving forward. At Weiser Family Farms we strive to provide the freshest and tastiest produce available. The many customers we serve at Farmers’ Markets throughout the Southland know they can count on us to deliver the best in specialty produce. The same applies to our wholesale customers and chefs from many of the area’s finer restaurants. A quality meal begins with quality ingredients. Weiser Farms understands this and strives to grow flavorful produce in an environmentally and health-friendly manner.

description: Beet Generation Farm exists to nourish the wellbeing of the farmer, the land, and the community. We grow responsibly cultivated and seriously delicious food, so that we may inspire & feed others from an authentic, kind-hearted core. From this place we believe that true kinship with the earth & one another are possible. We would love for you to join our CSA community or come say hi at the Santa Rosa Farmers Market – Saturday from 8:30AM-1PM @ 50 Mark West Springs Rd.

name: Fox Sparrow Farm
products: 100% Grass fed lamb, Heritage breed pork, and Heritage breed duck eggs.
description: We are a small livestock farm specializing in duck eggs, pork, and lamb. We pride ourselves on ethical, low stress handling. Our focus is preserving and supporting heritage breeds as well as growing a healthy animal above all else. We strive to be good stewards of the land we tend to by rotationally grazing our animals, having diverse livestock species that complement one another in a holistic approach, and providing habitat to native species whenever possible to uphold a healthy ecosystem. We are focused on sustainable and regenerative practices. Our ducks are all heritage breeds. We have over 10 different breeds that have different strengths such as foraging capabilities, mothering instincts, and egg color. I always describe duck eggs as chicken eggs on steroids. They are bigger and more nutrient dense, and I’m in love with their rich, velvety yolks. Our feed is GMO free. Our lamb is from two different hair sheep breeds. We raise American Blackbelly and Painted Desert sheep, both known for their hardiness, browsing capabilities, and delicious, mild tasting meat. During the dry season of California, these sheep not only deal with the heat much better than wool breeds, but they are also more than willing to browse on blackberry, willow, coyote bush… so when the grass is all gone, they can adapt. Our lamb is 100% grass/browse fed. Our pigs are heritage breed as well, right now we are raising a mix while we get started but our goal is to focus our attention on the  Gloucestershire Old Spot pigs, known for being excellent foragers and grazers, but also mothering instincts and mild temperament. We feed a mix of goat milk, GMO free grain, glean from orchards and gardens as well as walnuts seasonally.

description: We are a 17-acre organic farm in Fillmore, CA practicing regenerative agriculture. We are committed to drawing more carbon out of the atmosphere than putting carbon out into the environment. We bring back all the pre-consumer food waste from our restaurants back to the farm to be composted. We grow avocados, oranges, lemons, tomatoes, cucumbers, squash, peppers, eggplant, kale, swiss chard, cabbage, and herbs. We partner with Ayala Farms in Oxnard to produce our CSA collaboration boxes. $1 from every CSA box goes to Kiss the Ground.

name: Root 64 Sacramento

description: Root 64 Sacramento is a 1-acre urban farmstead in the Tallac Village neighborhood of Sacramento. We consciously grow food for our local community, using ecological methods to build and maintain healthy soil and to support a vibrant farm ecosystem. Our practices include:​​ No chemical applications: our inputs include OMRI listed compost, animal manures, & Diatomaceous Earth for pest control Soil preparation using a small walk-behind tractor & tarps Manual cultivation: weed control using hoes & other hand tools Minimal tillage Cover cropping & crop rotation Interplanting for efficient use of space & high diversity Straw mulching Shade cloth for season extension Drip irrigation for efficient water use Native & insectary plantings To get a taste of our farm products, drop by our Farm Stand on Saturdays from 9am to noon, April – November. Depending on the season you can also find our produce at several local restaurants.

name: Riverdog Farm

description: Riverdog Farm is a 450 acre certified organic, diversified family farm that grows vegetables, fruits, nuts, and raises chickens and pigs. We are located in the beautiful Capay Valley where rich creek-bottom soil, intense summer heat, and winter frost make exceptionally tasty fruits and vegetables. Since 1990 we have used a system of compost, crop rotation, cover cropping and hedgerow planting to keep our soil healthy and to promote a healthy ecosystem around our farm. Our animals are integrated into our farming system by providing natural fertilizer for orchards and fields and are all raised on organic pasture. Claim this listing!

description: We offer Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) memberships from our Arcata farm that provide Humboldt Bay area households with a weekly bounty of top-quality, ultra-fresh seasonal produce… Straight from our hands to yours! Eddie Tanner has been farming professionally in this area since 1999. Before starting DeepSeeded Farm in 2008, he was a manager of the UIHS Potawot Garden and the Arcata Educational Farm, and got his start in farming at Live Power Farm in Covelo.  He teaches gardening classes through HSU Extended Education, and is the author of “The Humboldt Kitchen Gardener,” a local gardening handbook. Claim this listing!

name: Sierra Valley Farms
products: ASPARAGUS BROCCOLI CABBAGE SPRING MIX SPINACH ARUGULA SORREL RADISHES CARROTS BEETS ROMAINE KALE HERBS GARLIC ONION HORSERADISH BEETS HEMP SWISS CHARD
description: Sierra Valley Farms is a 65-acre certified organic farm and nursery situated on the Middle Fork of the Feather River in the majestic Sierra Valley. The farm, located at 5,000 feet elevation, in Beckwourth California, has one of the most unique growing climates in the West. Sierra Valley Farms was first established as a native plant nursery in 1990 and broadened its diversity to growing certified organic produce in 1999. The family farm is owned and operated by Gary Romano. Sierra Valley Farms diverse operation includes growing and production of a wide range of cool-season vegetables and some fruits, micro greens, herbs, hops, and value-added condiments. The farm hosts an “on-farm” farmers market, restaurant CSA’s, and “Dinners in the Barn”. Sierra Valley Farms markets most of their products by way of Farmers Markets in the Reno/Tahoe area, and hosts the only On-farm Certified Farmers Market in California. The farm products are very popular in the community markets and also popular is the unique CSA program just for restaurants. Claim this listing!

name: Star Route Farms
products: Yellow squash, orange squash, coffee, dairy, cheese, salad greens, carrots
description: Star Route Farms began on five acres using horse-drawn sulky plows and cultivators and a lot of long haired ambition . As pioneers in the then fledgling organic industry we adopted production and post-harvest technologies–such as precision planters and hydrocooling equipment–in order to insure top quality produce for the consumer. Star Route Farms is the oldest continuously certified organic grower in California. The farm is presently certified by Marin Organic Certified Agriculture (MOCA).

description: The mission of The Noyo Food Forest is to cultivate a healthy local food system by creating opportunities for Fort Bragg youth and the Mendocino Coast community to learn about, grow, and access sustainably grown, garden-fresh foods. Noyo Food Forest is a 501(c)3 non-profit organization, donations are tax-deductible . EIN 76-0842972. THANK YOU FOR YOUR SUPPORT! Claim this listing!

name: Bramble Tail Homestead
products: Radishes, Turnips, Onions, lettuce and salad mix, arugula, kale, baby bok choi, colorful varieties of carrots, striped Armenian cucumbers, assorted heirloom tomatoes, scallions and onions, broccoli and cauliflower, fennel bulbs, eye-popping Galia melons
description: We believe in integrating ourselves with our ecosystem:  tending land via our relationship with animals, connecting to our place in the food chain with intimacy, and assisting folks in our community to participate in a truly local and connective way of eating. Bramble Tail Homestead is owned and operated by us – Aubrie Maze and Scott Kelley.  We have been living, working, traveling, raising animals and tending land together since 2010.  With Aubrie’s background in homesteading and herbalism, Scott’s background in mechanics and art, and our shared love of connection to place, we were both thrilled to discover that our skillsets lent themselves perfectly to a running a land-based business together. Claim this listing!

name: Laguna Farm
products: Spinach, beets, tangerines, celery, oranges, celery, cucumber, kale, fennel, chard, cilantro, berries, melon, apples, pears
description: Laguna Farm’s CSA program is the backbone of our farm business. With over 400 dedicated members, we are guaranteed to sell a great portion of our harvest to these loyal patrons. In turn, our CSA members get the best of what we have to offer. Every CSA program is as unique as the farmers themselves. We like to think of Laguna Farm as a very flexible CSA. We offer farm pick up, home delivery and neighborhood drop-site locations where members can find their produce at a location that suits them. Members can switch between these offerings with just one week notice. Laguna Farm features both produce and juicing boxes that contain a wide array of “in season” fruits and vegetables. We allow farm pick up members to trade out or exchange produce in their CSA box for items that may be more to their liking. Some of the trade options are limited, as we count on members to support the harvest, but we strive to accommodate different tastes and preferences. Claim this listing!

name: County Line Harvest
products: Carrots, Apples, Squash, Spinach, Lettuce, Celery Kale, Radishes, Melons, Tomatoes, Pepper
description: County Line Harvest began as six acres of farmland on the Sonoma-Marin County line in California. Today, we farm 35 acres in Petaluma year round, and 120 acres in Thermal over the winter season. We are incredibly grateful for our farm crews in Petaluma and Thermal who help cultivate our fields and harvest, pack, and transport our produce. We provide year-round employment for our core crew and seasonal work to an additional 35-40 people between our two locations. We are passionate about maintaining a safe and supportive environment for our farmers. We foster a safe workplace free of chemicals and support our farmers by offering flexible hours, access to education, job training, job advancement opportunities, and social service assistance. Claim this listing!

name: EarthSeed Farm
products: Asian Pears, Organic Apples, Persimmons, Raspberries, Pluots, Tomatoes, Pineapple Guavas, Blackberries, Lavender, Pumpkins, and Winter Squash
description: Established in March, 2021, EARTHseed Farm is a 14-acre solar-powered organic farm and orchard located in scenic Sonoma County, California. The farm is operated and rooted in Afro Indigenous permaculture principles and built on the long legacy of earth wisdom traditions of people of African descent. Permaculture is a relationship-based ecological design system embedded in indigenous wisdom that elevates ecosystem health while meeting human needs. Our farm is governed by a group of like-minded practitioners, where a variety of apples, pears, persimmons, plums, pluots, guavas, and mixed berries are grown. The farm is a working & learning environment offering land stewards and volunteers opportunities to learn how to honor wild tended areas, practical instruction in regenerative agricultural techniques, and modeling resilience practices.

name: Green Thumb Organics Farms

description: Providing healthy, organic food for his community is at the heart of Rudy Jimenez’s mission as a farmer. Growing up in a farmworker family, he founded Green Thumb Organics, a four-acre certified organic farm in San Juan Bautista, California, to do just that. In contrast to large-scale conventional farms in the area, Green Thumb Organics Farms sells produce direct to the public at farmers markets, like the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market in San Francisco, Via CUESA which has been instrumental in growing his farm business as well as Heart of The City Farmers Market. Claim this listing!

name: Live Earth Farm
products: Apples, apricots, strawberries, pears, grapes, basil, brussels sprouts, carrots, chard, collard, kale, etc.
description: Established as a Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) farm in 1995, we believe the key to growing nutritious (and tasty!) fruits and vegetables is creating and nurturing healthy soil. To do this we mimic natural soil-building processes using techniques such as composting, crop rotation, cover crops and mulching, adding organic soil amendments, and following careful tillage practices. These techniques allow us to grow and harvest food without depleting but instead nourishing the soil and its natural life cycle. As stewards of the land, we farm organically, and are certified organic by Organic Certifiers . Our overall farming philosophy includes growing our crops as close and harmonious with nature as possible. We thrive on building diversity to enhance the native habitat and organic ecosystem on the farm. We work with organizations like Wild Farm Alliance on establishing wildlife corridors, and ensure native plantings to improve water quality, reduce soil erosion, and create beneficial insect habitat.  A recent case study by California Climate & Agriculture Network determined “You would be hard pressed to find a better model of biodiversity and climate resilience than Live Earth Farm.” Claim this listing!

name: Dewlson Family Farm
products: Lemons, Coffee, Tea, Exotic Trees
description: We are a family farm, established in 2010. We grow Lisbon Lemons, five varieties of coffee, three varieties of tea, and many exotic fruits. Our lovely farm has easily accessible paths for walking with many spots to stop and enjoy the farm. We have tours by appointment.

name: Serendipity Farms
products: spinach, lettuce, arugula, strawberries or blueberries, and more!
description: Today Serendipity Farms raises more than 50 varieties of award-winning organic vegetables, herbs and flowers on 20 acres in Carmel Valley and Aromas. The different microclimates allow the farm to grow a huge variety of produce, from the fog zone-loving row crops, raspberries and strawberries grown on the historic Odello Ranch at the mouth of Carmel Valley to the inland heat lovers like tomatoes and basil that ripen on the mid-Valley parcel. On the homestead in Aromas are the Meyer lemon, avocado, figs and guava trees, plus the blackberries, tayberries and greenhouse-started herbs. In early 2014 the farm leased one acre of blueberries in Corralitos that will be certified organic in 2015. Do you own this farm? Claim listing below

name: Nourish Farm
products: salves, balms, tomatoes, zucchini, herbs, lamb, meat, peppers, flowers, bouquets, botanical oils, cucumbers, basil, carrots, onions, radishes, calendula, beets, lettuce
description: Nourish Farm is a small, family owned, first generation farm in Turlock, California. We provide sustainably grown, seasonal produce, herbs, flowers and pastured lamb meat to our community. We also create healing botanical products here at our farm. Our focus is creating a beautiful & healthy space to raise our family and nourish our community. Our farm is located in Turlock, California on a lovely 2 acre plot of land. In addition to growing delicious, seasonal produce, we raise sheep, chickens and pigs; and our sweet farm dog, Cosmo, & farm cat, Coco, run around all day greeting visitors at the gate and hunting gophers. Our farming philosophy is pretty simple: let nature do what it was intended to do. This means, we don’t till our soil, we don’t add synthetic fertilizers, we don’t use pesticides or herbicides; we try our best not to disturb the natural process and soil biology here on our land. We integrate our animals into our farming operation. Our crops and flowers are from non-GMO seeds, many of them heirloom or speciality varieties. Our goal is to grow beautiful, highly nutritious food for our community and ourselves. We love it here, and we’d love to have you come visit!

I grow a variety of produce including greens, root vegetables, culinary herbs, microgreens, beans, peas, cucumbers, squash, and more.

description: Our fathers came to California with a dream to provide a better future for their families. Working the fields from a very young age, they became the best at what they do. Fast forward to today; they run acres of agriculture spanning the Central Coast and beyond.

name: Durst Organic Growers
products: Cherry Tomatoes, Heirloom Tomatoes, Winter Squash, Pumpkins, Processing Butternut, Mixed Melons, Watermelon, Snap Peas, Asparagus, Green Beans, Alfalfa, Barley
description: We strive to produce and distribute fresh, organic, produce while serving as an educational, sustainable, and social network for our surrounding community. Our goal is to provide quality of life for the farmer and sustain economic viability for the farm with care and respect for nature’s diversity. Our fourth generation farm is located in an area of California called “Hungry Hollow” which is situated at the mouth of the Capay Valley in Yolo County. The unique microclimate and soils allow us to grow delicious tasting Asparagus, Melons, Watermelons, Cherry & Heirloom Tomatoes and Winter squash. Picked in the cool morning hours, packed and refrigerated immediately, we bring our products to your table in a “vine ripe” condition for superb flavor. From the beginning, Jim and Deborah have worked hard to build a conscious, ecologically minded business where both people and planet are treated respectfully. Great consideration for the health and wellbeing of Durst Organic Growers’ consumers and employees is taken when making every little decision in the growing of our crops. When you taste Durst produce, we hope you can taste the difference, because as Jim says, “If it doesn’t taste good, what’s the point?”

name: Capay Hills Orchard
products: Organic Almonds- raw, almond butter, smoked almonds, Mandarins, Naval Oranges, Grapefruit
description: We grow Certified Organic, California, truly raw, unpasteurized, almonds consumer and sell them direct to the consumer through our roadside stand and website! We are unique because we sell only our own almonds, and we harvest onto tarps, not the ground which eliminates exposure to harmful pathogens and the need to pasteurize. All equipment used is certified organic and free of other tree nuts, peanuts, grains etc. We practice regenerative, sustainable farming methods to ensure we are good stewards of our land. Our almonds are perfectly stored on site in a temperature and humidity controlled storeroom. We are a true family farm, all eight of us farm the property. We sell raw almonds (3 varieties available), smoked almonds from real wood smoke and stone-ground raw almond butter. Order direct from the farm website or feel free to call or text at 530 507-8222, we value direct relationships with our customers.

name: Talley Farms
products: Green beans, heirloom tomatoes, sweet peppers, winter and summer squash, raspberries, blackberries, lettuces, snap peas, celery, brussles sprouts, avocados, carrots, radishes, onions, kale, chard, potatoes, sweet potatoes, apples, pears
description: The Talley Family has been farming for over 70 years here on the Central California Coast. Currently, third generation Talley members manage the farm and winery while fourth generation Talleys work full time in key positions. We grow on 1700 acres in the Arroyo Grande and Edna Valleys with about 120 acres (and growing!) certified organic. We specialize in vegetable row crops, wine grapes (for Talley Vineyards,) avocados and lemons and are famous throughout the produce industry for our quality bell peppers. In 2012, we started a CSA program, and grow organically on approximately 120 acres of certified organic soil. Our CSA program sells directly to consumers located here on the Central Coast and throughout the Western United States. Our boxes contain only California grown produce, grown by us or other local, partner farms. Quality, Freshness and Value combined with strict food safety practices make our boxes the favorite CSA.

We have a neighborhood CSA program with drop off locations throughout the San Fransisco Bay area and peninsula, and hope to see you at one of our farmers’ markets. We use sustainable & organic practices to grow a little bit of everything that does well in our local climate: many varieties of tomatoes, peppers, corn, beans, peas, squash, cucumbers, lettuces, leafy greens, root crops, herbs, flowers, melons, strawberries, blenheim apricots and more. The farmers: Marsha and Modesto represent 3 continents and bring a mix of agroecological and traditional knowledge background to the farm. We are first generation farmers in this country, planting roots on the land to benefit our local community.

Approximately 1/4 acre, this diversified vegetable farm is located in an exciting, up and coming location in West Sacramento, directly next to the Barn in The Bridge District (TBD) at 985 Riverfront Street. The Barn is a phenomenal building which is not only an architectural gem but also houses Drakes Brewery and hosts a wide array of events throughout the year. Much of what is grown on the farm will be featured in the menu at Drakes. Riverfront Farm specializes in unique melons, veggies and herbs. Produce from this farm is grown without the use of chemicals and will focus on sustainable practices that are good for the earth and consumers.

description: Certified organic mixed vegetable farm.  Striving to do something positive in the world.  We practice as many regenerative farming techniques as possible.  We value the community of and around the farm more than anything.  We started in Bolinas, Ca as Big Mesa Farm and then relocated to a sweet mountain valley in the town of Comptche, Ca, just half hour from the coastal town of Mendocino.  We grow the best salad makings you can find, as well as root crops such as beets and carrots, and seasonal fruits like tomatoes and cucumbers.

The farm stand also offers corn meal, fresh masa, fresh and dried chiles and culinary gifts. CSA available; School Tours; Self-Guided Tours during Farm Stand hours. OPEN YEAR ROUND Rain or Shine. Farm stand open Thursday through Sunday.

We aim to give people a closer connection to the land and promote growing of open pollinated varieties of vegetables and fruits through direct contact with our customers through farmers markets and our mobile farmstand. We also sell to restaurants and small markets.

name: Alameda Point Collaborative Farm2Market
products: Strawberries, Mulberries, Apples, Stone Fruit, Asparagus, Honey, Flowers and many more seasonal fruits and vegetables
description: APC Farm2Market is a small, diversified working urban farm and a social enterprise of Alameda Point Collaborative. We use our passion for community, food and the environment to support APC residents as they move toward economic self-sufficiency and greater health and wellness. Our farm employs APC residents to work with staff and volunteers to produce delicious, nutritious fruits and veggies, raw honey and beautiful flowers. Proceeds from our CSA membership program are used to help sustain APC’s supportive housing community. Farm2Market consists of 2-acres of vegetable crops, fruit orchards, bee hives and flowers. We grow nearly everything from seed and strive to use sustainable practices, following permaculture principles and organic methods. We never use any chemical pesticides or fertilizers.

name: Prevedelli Farms
products: 40 Apple varieties/ 7 pear varieties/ 5 cane berries varieties/ Citrus/ Veggies/Plums/Prunes
description: Prevedelli Farm is a fourth-generation certified organic family run farm that has been operating in Watsonville since 1945, for over 75 years. The farm was originally established on Old San Jose Road in Soquel in the 1920s. It was started by Arturo Prevedelli, who emigrated from Italy in the early 1900s. A true family-run farm. The entire family works on the farm, whether it’s planting, harvesting, or selling at the farmer’s market: everybody is involved. All of the Prevedelli Farms’ fruit and vegetables are certified organically locally grown. Over 40 varieties of apples, 7 different types pears, and 5 types of berries are picked by hand at peak ripeness for full flavor. Berries are available in late spring and summer. Apples are harvested from July through November. The large variety of apples grown enables the Prevedelli Farms to keep up with the apple harvest, as they ripen at different times.

description: Formed in summer 2006 as a result of a Community Needs Assessment with initial seed funding from the Hub of Petaluma Foundation, Petaluma Bounty’s mission is to create a thriving local food system with healthy food for everyone through collaboration, education and promoting self-reliance.

name: Stonybrook Canyon Farm
products: tomatoes, melons, apples, pears, mulberries, and a couple dozen other products.
description: We are Stonybrook Canyon Farm in Castro Valley, along the Stonybrook Creek in Southern Alameda County. Our farm was established as a Pippin and Bellflower apple farm in the early 1900s and we have restored the property back to its original intentions. We grow a diverse array of products and sell directly to a a few high-end restaurants in the East Bay, along with operating a weekend farmstand. In December of 2019 we purchased another 155 acres of historic cherry orchard property and are now transitioning to a full-time and full-fledged farm. We are just getting started, so aren’t taking new customers yet, but we expect to be in full operation by summer of 2021.

description: We are a diversified family farm located in Nicasio, Marin County, within California’s North Coast region, producing rabbits, pigs and an assortment of poultry. Sustainable, humane agricultural practices are utilized, organic whenever possible.

description: Regenerative 1.5 acre farm using no-till, chemical-free practices. We specialize in Asian heritage vegetables and herbs. We sell our produce direct to chefs and our CSA in SF, East Bay and Sonoma County.

name: Oz Farm
products: We grow a wide variety of organic vegetables throughout the year including brassicas (broccoli, kale, cabbage etc), beets, onions, tomatoes, bush beans and much more. We also grow organic apples and pears, including many unusual heirloom
description: Oz Farm a certified organic farm, orchard and retreat center that trains beginning farmers each year through an educational apprenticeship. Oz is a multifaceted community that aspires to engage the public through immersive education in sustainable food systems and holistic life practices. Oz Farm is hidden in a quiet, private valley on one of the most pristine stretches of the scenic Mendocino County coast, 130 miles north of San Francisco. Bordered with redwood forest, and with the Garcia River running through its 240 acres, Oz Farm is ‘off-the-grid’, using solar and wind power for all its operations.

name: Duxberry Farm
products: Fruits , greens, Vegetables--pears, quince, figs, berries, processed products
description: small organic farm growing for production of Duxberry labeled products such as condiments, dried fruits, herbs, flavored salts and sugars. and flavored liqueurs. also specializing in selling plants for sale

name: Frog Hollow Farm
products: Peaches, Nectarines, Plums, Pluots, Apricots, Apriums, Cherries, Grapes, European Pears, Asian Pears, Apples, Pomegranate, Persimmon, Citrus, Olive Oil, Jam, Conserve, Pastries
description: Frog Hollow Farm is a 243-acre farm located in Brentwood, California. We grow legendary organic fruits and produce small-batch gourmet foods sold directly to consumers through our website, farmers’ market, CSA and our farm-to-table cafe. Our farm is home to hundreds of trees which produce peaches, nectarines, cherries, apricots, apriums, plums, pluots, Asian and European pears, olives, persimmons, quince, apples, meyer lemons, blood oranges and more. We are certified organic with C.C.O.F. (California Certified Organic Farmers) and committed to sustainable practices. Sustainability is an important value that Farmer Al has embraced since choosing to go organic in 1989. We steward our land with care and believe in treading lightly, so not only is the world a better, healthier place, but your neighbors and family are, too. In addition to our growing practices, we believe in sustainable labor practices. Many farms rely primarily on seasonal hires, and though our ranks swell during the harvest season as well, because we tend to our trees by hand and have a commercial kitchen on premises, we provide year-round employment for many local residents.

name: Pink Barn Farm
products: Lettuce, tomatoes, herbs, squash, onions, potatoes, peppers, cabbage, broccoli, kale, chard, cucumbers, spinach, eggplant
description: Pink Barn Farm is CSA and direct to wholesale farm in Sonoma County. We grow over 40 varieties of vegetables, herbs, and fruits. Our location and soil type allows us to grow throughout the entire year. We are planting and harvesting something new almost every week! Our farm system thrives on rich compost, gentle tillage, ample wildlife habitats, and lots of manual labor. We follow strict organic growing practices and value the health of the land above all else.

name: Common Roots Farm
products: Strawberries, raspberries, lettuce, cucumbers, summer and winter squash, hot and sweet peppers, tomatoes, dry-farmed tomatoes, melons, onions, beans, peas, dalias, zinnias, sunflowers, scabiosa, cosmos, strawflower, celosia, rudbekia, and filler flowers.
description: Common Roots is a low-till, non profit market farm located on 4 acres approximately 3/4 mile from downtown Santa Cruz. We employ ecological practices and steward a riparian habitat that runs along one perimeter of our property. Our farm welcomes farmers with developmental disabilities and serves our local community with a diverse assortment of vegetables, berries, and cut flowers for market bouquets. We have a weekend farm stand, small CSA, and also produce value-added products from our strawberries, tomatoes and peppers. We also have a sprint plant sale with vegetable and flower starts.

name: Shakefork Community Farm
products: Most garden staples such as lettuce, spinach, greens, cucumbers, zucchini, potatoes, tomatoes, peppers, onions, peas and more, strawberries and herbs; pasture-raised, organically fed chicken, turkey and eggs; grass-fed beef.
description: Oxen powered produce and pasture raised meats and eggs. Not certified organic, but holding to the highest standards in regenerative agriculture including low-till practices in the garden and intensively managed, multi-species grazing using the principles of holistic management. We produce all of our own compost on site.

name: Birdsong Orchards
products: Peaches, plums, apricots, figs, apples, pears, citrus, roses, flowers, walnuts, cherries, guava, pluots, plumcots, nectarines, ume.
description: Birdsong Orchards is an organic fruit and flower farm on the California coast focused on regenerative agriculture. We celebrate diversity with over 300 varieties of fruit trees and flowering perennials. Our goal is to encourage bio-diversity and environmental balance while growing produce of the highest quality and taste. Why do we do it? – To show that agriculture and nature can co-exist in harmony. – To prove that small scale organic farming can be viable. – To provide hope in the face of climate crisis. – To create a template for local farming in uncertain times.

name: Veggielution
products: Tomatoes, peppers, corn, potatoes, kale, radishes, carrots, kale, cabbage, chayote, cauliflower, squash, cucumbers, cilantro, epazote, rosemary, basil, parsley, plums, peaches, applies, pears, apricots, persimmons, pomegranates, mulberries
description: Veggielution is a 6-acre urban farm located in East San José. We currently offer produce grown onsite through our weekly farm stand, farm box distribution to low-income families, and hot meal delivery to COVID-impacted seniors and other vulnerable individuals.

name: Coyote Family Farm
products: Weekly farm share box; lettuce, tomatoes, peppers, broccoli, melons, strawberries, kale, chard, scallions, onions, carrots, beets, radishes, turnips, cucumbers, zucchini, basil, parsley, cauliflower, dahlias, zinnias, ranunculus, anemeon
description: We are a 2-acre intensive market garden located at the foot of Sonoma Mountain between two watersheds. We use ecological methods to build soil and grow nutritious food. We grow a diversity of vegetable and flower crops for our farm share, a local farmers market, and local wholesale.

name: Chiatri de Laguna Farm
products: Apples Berries Figs Grapes Melons Corn Cucumber Eggplant Kale Peppers Potatoes Pumpkins Squash - Summer Squash - Winter Tomatoes Cut flowers
description: Chiatri de Laguna, formerly Chiatri USA and Grossi Egg Ranch, was founded in the mid 1940’s by Dino & Thelma Grossi, who grew up in this neighborhood. They built an egg ranch, raised most of their own food and a family. They were Farm Trails members and sold eggs and produce on site for many years. Our goal is to honor this legacy by creating a place of beauty and abundance, to serve the community and be a “hamlet” as is Chiatri in Italy. A seasonal farm stand offers vegetables and fruit, continuing its history of on-farm sales.

name: Red H Farm
products: Lettuce, Greens, Dry-Farmed Heirloom Tomatoes, Persian Cucumbers, Heirloom Summer Squash, Onions, Shallots, Winter Squash, Broccoli, Cauliflower, Cabbage
description: Red H Farm is a 1.2 acre agroecological farm focused on soil health, water conservation, biodiversity, social equity and civic engagement. We grow diversified vegetables using hand-scale systems. Our produce is available at the Sebastopol Farmers Markets and through our upcoming winter CSA.

name: Kiss the Flower Honey Co.
products: Honey, Honeycomb, Bee Pollen
description: Kiss the Flower Honey Co. produces wildflower, blackberry and Star Thistle honey from beehives throughout Sonoma County. In addition we offer honeycomb, bee pollen, beeswax and propolis tinctures.
